headline: CORRECTION: July PPI was actually flat/cool (core +0.2% vs +0.3% est.), not hot as reported in yesterday's evening briefs
gist: First run of the day. Correcting an error in the 18:30 and 21:26 IST Aug 13 briefs, which reported a 'hot' July PPI (+0.9% m/m/+3.3% y/y) driving a hawkish Fed repricing and gold's fade. Verified directly against the BLS primary source (bls.gov PPI release, Aug 13 2026): headline PPI for final demand was actually UNCHANGED (flat) in July; core PPI (ex food/energy) rose just +0.2% m/m, below the +0.3% consensus estimate; annual headline PPI cooled to 4.7% y/y from 5.5% in June. This is a materially different, dovish read -- multiple corroborating sources (Axios, ZeroHedge, TradingKey, CNBC, NBC) confirm the cooler print eased September Fed rate-hike pressure (CME FedWatch showed a 62% hold probability pre-release) and sent US equities to fresh records: S&P 500 +0.65-0.7% (record high), Nasdaq +0.8%, Dow +0.1% on Thursday Aug 13. Despite the dovish/bullish-for-gold framing, Gold and Silver extended their overnight slide anyway (see companion item) -- best explained as safe-haven demand rotating into the risk-asset rally (record-high equities) rather than a rates story, since DXY (~99.87) and 10Y yields (~4.66-4.74%) stayed firm rather than falling as a dovish reprice would suggest. Flagging this correction for the group's accuracy; the earlier 'hot PPI' framing sent Aug 13 was incorrect. Source: BLS (bls.gov/news.release/archives/ppi_08132026.htm)/Axios/ZeroHedge/TradingKey/CNBC/NBC News. Sent with cards (bias board, news, Gold chart).
